name: showreel-47-user-invalid
style: A sign-up form that is already red before anyone types: three fields lit like warning lamps flare, the counter reads 3, then user-invalid keeps it dark until the finger leaves a field (black look, a blue accent).

voice.text: Why is it red before typing? Empty fields count as invalid from the start. So the form paints red at once. The fix: swap invalid for user invalid. Now red waits until you leave the field.

caption:
Why is your form red before you type anything? 🔴 You open it and every field is already shouting.

An empty required field counts as invalid from the first paint, so input:invalid colours it at once. The fix: style input:user-invalid instead. It matches only after the person has interacted with the field, so the red waits until they leave it with a bad value. MDN: :user-invalid matches an invalid control after the user has interacted with it. Chrome 119, Firefox 88, Safari 16.5 (MDN browser compatibility).

Watch the counter: RED FIELDS reads 3 before the fix and 0 after it.

Save it for your next sign-up form, or send it to whoever builds yours.

sources.note: MDN :user-invalid (page source mdn/content, read 25 Nov 2026): represents any validated form element whose value isn't valid based on its validation constraints, after the user has interacted with it; it must match an :invalid, :out-of-range, or blank-but :required element between the time the user has attempted to submit the form and before the user has interacted again with the form element
MDN BCD css.selectors.user-invalid (read 25 Nov 2026): Chrome 119, Edge 119, Firefox 88, Safari 16.5

tip.title: Why is your form red before you type anything?
tip.why: An empty required field is invalid from the first paint, so an input:invalid rule colours it red before anyone has touched the form. input:user-invalid matches the same fields only after the person has interacted with them (MDN: an invalid control after the user has interacted with it), so the red waits until they leave a field with a bad value. Supported in Chrome 119, Firefox 88 and Safari 16.5 (MDN browser compatibility data).
tip.code:
<input required>
<input type="email" required>

/* red before anyone types */
input:invalid { border-color: red; }

/* red only after the person has interacted */
input:user-invalid { border-color: red; }
